question: Is the trouble lane's surface a SIXTH PANE on the web interface, or a CHANNEL of the console pane? Every other answer in that design hangs off this one, which is why the node could not cast.
whats_beyond: Akien's own 2026-08-11 ruling makes Murderbot's pane set the channel set — status, settings (with circuit breaker), console (INFO default / DEBUG), chat — which argues CHANNEL. His idea as captured says 'i can see them on the web interface as we've already designed it', which reads either way. It is a one-sentence ruling from him and it unblocks a whole design; it is not a thing to derive. Constraint either way: ONE web server, a device gets a DECLARED PANE and never its own route/port/server — and whether the surface can carry a declared pane TODAY is itself unmeasured.

resolved.answer: A trouble ticket PANEL (new pane). Two-sided: list at left, detail at right. Red light at top — bright red if live troubles, dull reddish grey if none. Right side shows contents of selected trouble. Starts at row 0 on first load. Dynamic page. Lives on the cairn device (the all-of-cairn singleton, ruled same session). Base panels are not all the panels — override/add is fine.
resolved.source: Akien, 2026-08-19: "we add a trouble ticket panel. two sides. a list at the left. on the right a red light at the top..."
resolved.open_edge: framework question: current web server is stdlib http.server + pure render, no client-side JS. The dynamic panel needs interaction (click-to-select, live refresh). htmx or inline JS — decision deferred, not blocking the panel design.
